Shortcut Menu turns your choice of accessibility services on and off from the accessibility shortcut, such as holding both volume keys. With a screen reader on, the menu is a list that the screen reader reads. With none on, it speaks for itself: drag your finger to hear the choices, and lift it to choose. Turning a screen reader on turns any other screen reader off. If your screen reader or your phone\'s speech stops working, press volume up three times quickly in the menu for safe mode: it turns screen readers off and speaks the menu in its own voice, so you can turn one back on.
Granted. Shortcut Menu can turn services on and off.
Android only lets apps turn accessibility services on and off with a permission that you grant once, from a computer with adb, or with Shizuku. Run this command:

In Accessibility settings, open Shortcut Menu and turn on its shortcut. Make Shortcut Menu the only feature on that shortcut. With more than one, Android asks which one to use, and that question is not spoken without a screen reader.
Android\'s question the first time the volume key shortcut is used is marked as answered, so the shortcut works at once.
